title.narrative: Supporting Fiscal and Economic Recovery Program (Subprogram 1)

description.narrative: The Supporting Fiscal and Economic Recovery Program will help the Government of Solomon Islands implement reforms to support a resilient economic and fiscal recovery from the contraction caused by the coronavirus disease pandemic. The proposed program comprises two subprograms to promote (i) tax reform for domestic revenue mobilization, (ii) public financial management for fiscal resilience, and (iii) an enabling environment for private sector recovery.

Output/s as listed by the project staff.
1.1. To modernize tax administration and unify the framework for different taxes, the Parliament passed a new Tax Administration Act 2022

1.10. To fight corruption and improve the business environment, the government operationalized the Solomon Islands Independent Commission Against Corruption (SIICAC), through 1.10.1. establishment of an annual budget allocation for SIICAC starting with the 2021 government budget, and appropriation of funds in 2021 and 2022; s and 1.10.2. approval by the Prime Minister of the Solomon Islands the Solomon Islands Independent Commission Against Corruption (Renumeration and Other conditions) Regulations 2020 effective October 2020 outlining the remuneration of the SIICAC Commissioners.

1.2. To remove distortions and raise revenue in a more efficient manner, the cabinet approved 1.2.1. a policy to provide the basis for the preparation of a broad-based value-added tax bill; and 1.2.2. drafting instructions for the Attorney General's Chambers to prepare a value-added tax bill

1.3. To ensure there are sufficient resources to administer collections from the largest taxpayers, 1.3.1. the Minister of Finance and Treasury approved the establishment of a new Large Taxpayers' Office (LTO), as an integral part of the new functional-based IRD restructure; and 1.3.2. MOFT began to operationalize the LTO by appointing staff to at least 20% of the approved positions, of whom at least 40% are female.

1.4. To raise revenue and improve development outcomes, the Minister for Finance and Treasury made the Customs and Excise (Import Duties) (Amendment) Order 2021 and the Customs and Excise (Import Duties) (Amendment) (No. 2) Order 2021 and MOFT implemented 1.4.1. a new tax on sugar and sugary drinks to improve health outcomes by discouraging sugar consumption, and raise revenue; d and 1.4.2. a new tax on single-use plastics and other plastics with toxic components to reduce plastic pollution

1.5 To improve debt management arrangements, the cabinet approved effective July 2021 and MOFT published on its website an MTDMS 2021-2024, which includes financing strategies and debt service requirements.

1.6. To improve the governance of public spending, the 1.6.1 Minister for Finance and Treasury issued effective October 2021, the Public Financial Management (Procurement) Regulations 2021, which include a principle that procurement activities support equality of opportunity and provide economic opportunities for women, youth and people with disabilities; k and operations as required by the PFM Act (2013). 1.6.2 Permanent Secretary of MOFT approved effective April 2022 a new comprehensive Financial Controllers' Operations Manual that specifies the responsibilities of Financial Controllers across line ministries to enable more effective management of public financial
1.7. To establish the legal framework to introduce a modern payments infrastructure and regulatory system, the Parliament passed a Payment Systems Act 202

1.8. To understand the opportunities and risks related to financial sector development and increase women's financial inclusion, the 1.8.1. Solomon Islands Financial Inclusion Taskforce, chaired by the Governor of the CBSI, approved effective August 2022 the National Women's Financial Inclusion Policy 2022-2026 which sets clear targets, measures and actions to guide reforms; p and 1.8.2. cabinet approved a new Financial Institutions Act policy paper that (i) will guide further consultation; (ii) includes specific recommendations based on a gender gap analysis; and (iii) provides a strong basis for new legislation that will strengthen the regulation and prudential supervision of financial institutions.

1.9. To improve the governance of SOEs, the cabinet approved a policy paper that provides a strong basis for the preparation of an SOE act amendment bill to (i) align with the SOE Ownership Policy (2018), q (ii) consolidate responsibility and oversight of SOEs to the Minister for Finance and Treasury, (iii) strengthen SOEs' publication and transparency requirements, and (iv) provide for promotion of gender diversity among SOE staff and board members
